introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Information and Communication Technologies 2 (0796), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be graded on your ability to use good English, organise information clearly and the use of specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A project schedule is given below

| Task | Predecessor | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| A | - | 3 |
| B | - | 2 |
| C | A | 4 |
| D | B | 1 |
| E | D | 2 |
| F | B | 3 |
| G | C | 2 |

(a) What is a task? (1 mark)

(b) Represent the schedule above in a Gantt chart. (3 marks)

(c) Determine the critical path. (2 marks)

(d) Determine any slack task if it exists. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Task (1 mark).** A task (activity) is a distinct piece of work in a project, with a start, an end and a duration, that must be completed to finish the project. It may depend on other tasks (its predecessors) that must be finished before it can start.

**(b) Gantt chart (3 marks).** A Gantt chart is a bar chart with the tasks listed down the left side and the time along the top; the length of each bar is the duration of the task and each task is drawn at its earliest start time (a task starts when all its predecessors are finished). The durations are not given with a unit; they are shown here in days.

| Task | Duration | Earliest start | Earliest finish | Latest start | Latest finish | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| B | 2 | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 4 |
| C | 4 | 3 | 7 | 3 | 7 | 0 |
| D | 1 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 7 | 4 |
| E | 2 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 | 4 |
| F | 3 | 2 | 5 | 6 | 9 | 4 |
| G | 2 | 7 | 9 | 7 | 9 | 0 |

![fig-1](gce-al-ict-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

A and B start together at time 0; C starts after A (time 3); D and F start after B (time 2); E starts after D (time 3); G starts after C (time 7). The whole project takes **9 days**. The drawing may also be done on a grid in which each task is a row and each day a column, with the bar shaded from the start day to the finish day.

**(c) Critical path (2 marks).** The critical path is the longest path through the tasks, which fixes the minimum time for the project. The three paths are:

- A - C - G : 3 + 4 + 2 = 9
- B - D - E : 2 + 1 + 2 = 5
- B - F : 2 + 3 = 5

The longest path is **A - C - G**, so the critical path is A - C - G and the project lasts 9 days. Any delay on A, C or G delays the whole project.

**(d) Slack (1 mark).** Slack (float) is the time a task can be delayed without delaying the end of the project. Tasks A, C and G are critical (slack 0). The tasks **B, D, E and F** have slack: each can be delayed by **4 days** (9 - 5 = 4) without delaying the project; this slack is shared by the tasks of the same path (B, D, E, or B and F).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two examples of interfaces are GUI, and command line (CL) interfaces.

(a) What is an operating system interface? (1 mark)

(b) State two characteristics of GUI. (1 mark)

(c) Give two reasons why the GUI is commonly used than the CL interface. (2 marks)

(d) Give one advantage of command line over GUI. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Operating system interface (1 mark).** The interface is the part of the operating system that lets the user communicate with the computer: it accepts the user's instructions and shows the results and messages.

**(b) Two characteristics of a GUI (1 mark).**

- It is made of windows, icons, menus and a pointer (WIMP), so it is based on pictures and not on typed text.
- It is operated with a pointing device (mouse, touch screen) and the user can have several windows open at the same time.

**(c) Two reasons why the GUI is more commonly used (2 marks).**

- It is easy to learn and to use, because the user clicks on icons and menus and does not need to remember commands.
- It is attractive and intuitive: what the user does (dragging a file, previewing a document) is shown on the screen, so beginners make fewer mistakes.

**(d) One advantage of the command line (1 mark).** A command-line interface needs less memory and processing power and runs faster on a small computer; experts can also give precise commands and combine them in scripts to automate tasks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A printer is one of the main output devices.

(a) State TWO characteristics that determine the quality of a printer. (1 mark)

(b) State two categories of printers and in each category give an example. (3 marks)

(c) How can we measure the speed of a printer? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two characteristics that determine the quality (1 mark).** The **resolution** (the number of dots per inch, dpi) and the **colour capability** (the number of colours it can print). (Also: the quality of the ink or toner and of the paper.)

**(b) Two categories of printers (3 marks).**

- **Impact printers**, which print by striking an inked ribbon against the paper; example: the **dot-matrix printer** (also daisy-wheel, line printer).
- **Non-impact printers**, which print without hitting the paper (ink spray, laser light and toner, or heat); example: the **laser printer** (also inkjet, thermal printer).

**(c) Speed of a printer (2 marks).** The speed is measured in **pages per minute (ppm)** for page printers such as laser and inkjet printers, and in **characters per second (cps)** (or lines per minute, lpm) for dot-matrix and line printers.
